items.text: All inputs and their weighted average must lie in the same interval on which f is convex or concave.
Weights are nonnegative and sum to one; arbitrary coefficients do not define a convex combination.
For strictly convex f and positive weights, equality holds exactly when all inputs are equal. With non-strict convexity, f may be affine on the span of the inputs.

items.text: Check whether f is convex or concave before choosing the direction of Jensen's inequality.
A sign change in the second derivative may mean the chosen interval is too large for a single Jensen step.
Strict convexity is what supports the usual all-inputs-equal equality claim; ordinary convexity alone may have additional equality cases.
